subject: Electrical Engineering
title: LEDs: Light from a Junction
description: One-minute skill: LEDs: Light from a Junction.

hook.text: When electrons fall into holes at a PN junction, they can release energy as light.

buildup.text: The color depends on the band gap. Gallium arsenide glows red. Indium gallium nitride glows blue.

discovery.text: Blue LEDs were the missing piece. With red, green, and blue, white light became possible.

twist.text: The 2014 Nobel Prize went to three scientists for cracking the blue LED problem.

climax.text: LED bulbs use 75% less energy than incandescent lights and last 25 times longer.

punchline.text: Electrons drop into holes, photons fly out — a junction that glows.

quiz.question: What determines the color of light an LED emits?
options: The amount of current flowing through the LED
The band gap energy of the semiconductor material used
The physical size and shape of the LED chip
